content.value_statement: Researchers need a repeatable way to turn datasets and papers into testable hypotheses. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Hypogenic workflows for generation, inference, and evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Guides data-driven hypothesis generation from labeled observational datasets.
Explains HypoGeniC, HypoRefine, and union method workflows.
Documents required dataset structure and configuration templates.
Shows CLI and Python API paths for generation and inference.
Covers optional literature PDF preprocessing with GROBID.
Describes evaluation, caching, parallel processing, and adaptive refinement.
limitations: Requires the external hypogenic package and separate datasets.
Needs user-provided API credentials or configured local models.
Literature workflows require GROBID, valid PDFs, and preprocessing steps.
Generated hypotheses need expert review before research conclusions.

use_cases.title: Explore New Research Datasets
use_cases.description: Generate candidate hypotheses from labeled examples before formal modeling or manual theory development.

use_cases.title: Combine Papers with Observations
use_cases.description: Use literature-backed workflows to compare theory-based hypotheses with patterns found in data.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Hypothesis Methods
use_cases.description: Run generation, inference, and evaluation workflows across datasets to compare hypothesis quality.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Initial Hypotheses
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a prepared labeled dataset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Hypogenic to plan a basic data-driven hypothesis generation run for my dataset. Include required files, configuration fields, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Custom Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for adapting a new dataset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me adapt Hypogenic for a new binary classification task. Describe the dataset format, label extraction needs, prompts, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Literature Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using HypoRefine with papers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a HypoRefine workflow that combines ten research papers with my observational dataset. Include preprocessing, hypothesis generation, and comparison steps.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Hypothesis Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for benchmarking and iteration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evaluation plan for Hypogenic outputs. Compare hypothesis diversity, accuracy, inference behavior, and failure cases across multiple methods.

output_examples.input: A researcher has labeled examples of human and AI-written text.
output: A setup plan for data-driven HypoGeniC generation.
A list of required training, validation, and test files.
Suggested review criteria for generated language-pattern hypotheses.

output_examples.input: A team wants to combine deception detection papers with review data.
output: A HypoRefine workflow covering paper preprocessing and dataset preparation.
A comparison plan for literature-only and data-driven hypotheses.
Evaluation guidance for accuracy, diversity, and practical usefulness.

output_examples.input: An engineer needs to benchmark several hypothesis generation methods.
output_examples.output: The skill can outline generation runs, inference passes, result comparisons, and follow-up checks for weak or redundant hypotheses.

best_practices: Start with clean labels and consistent feature fields across train, validation, and test splits.
Review generated hypotheses for specificity, falsifiability, and domain relevance before inference.
Pin external dependencies and record model settings for reproducible experiments.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated hypotheses as validated scientific conclusions.
Do not mix label formats between datasets and extraction logic.
Do not run unreviewed setup commands or external scripts in sensitive environments.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and run Hypogenic workflows for LLM-based hypothesis generation, refinement, inference, and evaluation.

faq.question: Does it include datasets or the Hypogenic package?
faq.answer: No. It documents how to install the package and use external example datasets.

faq.question: Can it use research papers?
faq.answer: Yes. HypoRefine workflows can use preprocessed literature PDFs together with empirical data.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are generated hypotheses automatically correct?
faq.answer: No. They are candidates that require testing, expert review, and careful interpretation.

faq.question: What should I check before running commands?
faq.answer: Review package sources, repository URLs, script contents, credentials, and the environment where commands will run.
